prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the layout of an indoor mall corridor and dual escalators, showing the floor receding smoothly from under 1 m in the bottom foreground to over 10 m in the dark background, alongside pillars (2–4 m away in frame 1), railings, and ascending escalator balustrades. A companion in a white shirt and mask stands 1–1.5 m to the right in frame 1, moves 2–2.5 m ahead and to the left in frame 2 (with another passerby 4–5 m to the right and distant figures 8–10 m behind), returns to within 1 m on the right in frames 3–4, and steps onto the right escalator 1–1.5 m directly ahead and slightly above the wearer in frame 5. The companion is within arm's reach of the camera wearer in frames 1, 3, 4, and 5 and holds the escalator handrail within his own arm's reach in frame 5, while his lower body and right side are partly cropped by the frame edges in frames 1, 3, 4, and 5. Compared to RGB alone, the continuous luminance gradients make the 3D geometry of the floor plane, pillar, and escalator steps immediately separable from surface textures and bright shop lighting. However, the depth map is unreliable along the left edge of frame 3 where a false bright band appears, on the dark escalator steps in frame 3 which blend into the distant background, and on the companion's silhouette where facial orientation and gaze direction toward the wearer in frames 1 and 4 are completely lost.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates foreground and mid-ground people from the unlabelled mall structure, tracking the main companion in pink on the far right at 1–1.5 m in frame 1 (partly out of view), full-body on the left at 2–2.5 m in frame 2, on the right at 0.8–1.2 m in frames 3 and 4 (cropped at the right and bottom edges), and ahead on the escalator at 1–1.5 m in frame 5 (cropped at the top). In frame 2, it also segments a walking person in brown 4–5 m to the right (about 3 m from the companion) and three distant figures 6–10 m away in the background (1–3 m apart from each other), while in frame 5 it detects a bystander 5–6 m away to the upper right on the main floor. While the mask contours indicate that the companion turns from facing left/toward the wearer in frame 1 to facing away in frame 2, left in frame 3, toward the wearer in frame 4, and away up the escalator in frame 5 (within the wearer's arm's reach in frames 1 and 3–5), internal facial features and exact gaze are not preserved. This map makes it easier than RGB to spot small, distant pedestrians in the cluttered background of frames 2 and 5 and clearly delineates the boundary of the companion against bright shopfronts. However, it is highly unreliable for objects, hallucinating a giant 'suitcase' mask over the central escalator divider at 1.5–3 m in frame 4, misclassifying a decorative cow statue and sign at 6–8 m as two 'chair' instances and a floor decal at 3 m as a 'skateboard' in frame 2, and missing the escalators, railings, and several background pedestrians entirely.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank across frames 1, 3, 4, and 5, providing a 2D body skeleton only in frame 2 for the companion standing 2–2.5 m ahead and to the left of the camera wearer. In frame 2, the yellow torso, limb, and head keypoints show the companion upright, facing away and slightly left toward the distant corridor, with his head turned in profile and not looking at the camera wearer, and his hands hanging near his hips out of the wearer's arm's reach. Because no other skeletons are rendered, the map provides no spatial information about the mall layout, the escalators, or the other pedestrians standing 4–10 m away to the right and in the background, nor does it capture the companion's approach and boarding of the escalator in frames 3–5. Where present in frame 2, the skeleton makes the exact joint articulation of the companion's shoulders, elbows, hips, and knees under his loose clothing and the leftward yaw of his head clearer than in the RGB image alone. However, the map is largely unreliable across the sequence because it fails to detect the companion whenever his body is partially occluded by the right, bottom, or top frame boundaries at close range (1–1.5 m) in frames 1, 3, 4, and 5, misses all distant people, and omits magenta hand skeletons entirely even when the companion's hands are visible near his face in frame 1 or gripping the handrail in frame 5.
